subject: EU node operator reassignment — custody mapping & migration window
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: platform-ops@globex.com, sandra.lang@globex.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: EU node operator reassignment — custody mapping & migration window

Hi Sandra / Platform Ops team,

Quick heads-up: as part of our ongoing cost and reliability improvements we are reassigning the EU edge/node operator for a subset of Regions (eu-central-1 and eu-west-2) from ArborCloud to NodalEdge. This change is operational only — no model changes — but it does introduce a new subprocessor (NodalEdge) that will handle transient KV cache and GPU-backed ephemeral disk for inference sessions.

Action items for Globex:
- Please confirm whether you require a signed subprocessor addendum or an updated vendor roster entry for procurement.
- Let us know if you need the SOC2 evidence for NodalEdge or an updated custody mapping for PII/Logs within the EU.
- We propose a migration window: 2027-05-10 to 2027-05-14 with a canary on 2027-05-10. If that window doesn't work, provide alternatives.

I've attached a preliminary "redwood-eu-operator-mapping-v1.pdf" that shows which services will touch customer data and how custody is handed off. Also attached is our latest SOC2 summary for Redwood; NodalEdge's SOC2 is available on request — we are coordinating that.

High-level mitigations:
- Traffic will be routed by region policy; nodes will only be promoted after KV cache warm-up benchmarks pass.
- Canary runs will be restricted to 5% of traffic for 24 hours with automatic rollback on error spike or latency regression.
- We will provide logs and audit samples in the Drive folder linked below for your team and security reviewers.

If you prefer, I can schedule a 30-minute sync with our infrastructure lead to walk through the playbook and the canary plan.

Thanks,
Diego
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
Diego Fernandez | diego.fernandez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood-eu-operator-mapping-v1.pdf, soc2-report-2026.pdf
Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_exAMPLE/redwood-globex-eu-transition

From: Sandra Lang <sandra.lang@globex.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, platform-ops@globex.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 12:30:00 +0200
Subject: Re: EU node operator reassignment — custody mapping & migration window

Diego, thanks for the early notice. A few questions from our side before we greenlight a window: 

1) NodalEdge SOC2 status: do they have an external report we can review or an attestation? We need at least SOC2 Type II or equivalent for processors handling ephemeral storage in the EU.
2) Data custody: per the mapping you sent, are customer logs (request/response traces) ever persisted outside eu-west-2/eu-central-1? Our regulator requires strict residency for trace data tied to user identifiers.
3) Retention and deletion: during the canary we need a documented retention policy and verification steps showing that ephemeral cache entries are purged within X minutes after session end.

We can provision a short review with our security/compliance team — they prefer to see the vendor questionnaire filled (we can share our questionnaire) plus access to the playbook and a sample of audit logs. If NodalEdge SOC2 is not yet available, a signed DPIA or equivalent mitigations with documented controls may suffice for short-lived canary traffic.

Our preferred migration window is 2027-05-17 to 2027-05-21 to avoid other internal releases. Can you confirm whether that alternate window is acceptable?

If useful, loop in your infra and legal; we will CC our security@example.com alias for the review.

Best,
Sandra
Platform Operations Manager, Globex Financial Services
platform-ops@globex.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: EU node operator reassignment — custody mapping & migration window

Diego / team,

Summary / proposed deliverables for Globex security review:

1) NodalEdge package: vendor contact, current compliance posture (SOC2 Type II if available, otherwise SOC2 Type I + DPIA + compensating controls), signed subprocessor addendum, and evidence of encrypted-at-rest for ephemeral disks. We will request their "SOC-related control matrix" and map their controls to Globex's questionnaire.

2) Data custody statement: one-page statement confirming that request/response traces containing user identifiers will remain in eu-west-2 / eu-central-1 and that aggregated telemetry (no user identifiers) may be replicated for monitoring but only in pseudonymized form. I will draft this.

3) Canary playbook: provide "eu-migration-playbook.xlsx" with a checklist: pre-checks, canary traffic gating (5%), monitoring thresholds (error rate + latency SLOs), retention verification steps (sample purge verification), rollback triggers, post-canary reporting. Vivek, please fill the monitoring thresholds and rollback steps inline.

4) Timeline: we can accept Globex's preferred window 2027-05-17 to 05-21 if Vivek confirms no infra conflicts. If NodalEdge cannot produce SOC2 Type II by then, we will require a signed time-limited exception with extra monitoring and a contract clause mandating SOC2 delivery within 90 days post-migration.

5) Communication: schedule a 30-minute joint session with Globex security this week. Diego, please propose two 30-min slots.

I will start drafting the data custody statement and the vendor package request email to NodalEdge. Assigning tasks:
- Marissa: vendor package and custody statement (owner)
- Vivek: monitoring thresholds, rollback checklist (owner)
- Lauren: procurement/contract language for time-limited exception and subprocessor addendum (owner)

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: eu-migration-playbook.xlsx (to follow), vendor-attestation-template.docx
